incidents.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.title_en: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition
incidents.summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, is suing Fargo, North Dakota, and detective Lucas Heck for $10m after being falsely arrested and jailed for six months. She was taken at gunpoint from her home in July 2025 while babysitting four children, then held nearly four months without bail in Tennessee and about two more months in North Dakota on theft and identity fraud charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud occurred, and she was released on Christmas Eve.

The lawsuit says Fargo police relied on an AI facial recognition match from a fake ID and a social media photo, although Lipps did not resemble the suspect and had never been there. It alleges Heck sought a warrant without probable cause and that the department lacked facial recognition policies and training. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and belongings and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation, and the lawsuit seeks damages and accountability.

incidents.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife
incidents.title_en: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife
incidents.summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors: unauthorized computer access and fraud, repeated annoying phone calls, and contempt of court for violating a restraining order. After his mistress ended their relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in a day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in one day. He also made 13 improper searches in a state law enforcement database on his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used a license plate reader system to track their vehicles.

Josett was served with an emergency protective order and a notice of intent to terminate on June 28, 2024, but then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years of informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, after already spending nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review by California's Peace Officers Standards and Training is still pending.

incidents.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.title_en: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal
incidents.summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing the city of Española after what they say was an unlawful traffic stop. On July 23, a Flock Safety camera misread the license plate of Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, reading a final digit 2 as 7 and flagging her car as stolen from Rio Rancho. Police pulled her over on Calle Duran, handcuffed her and her 12-year-old sister, and placed both in separate police cars before realizing the error. Jaclynn asked an officer to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers handcuffed the child anyway.

The sisters filed lawsuits on Jan. 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, who was 17 when he was stopped in April after being mistakenly linked to an armed robbery. The city, police chief, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits are now pending in state District Court.

incidents.title: Russia Aims to Inject Chaos Into Elections, U.S. Intelligence Finds
incidents.title_en: Russia Aims to Inject Chaos Into Elections, U.S. Intelligence Finds
incidents.summary:
U.S. officials say Russia has been running covert online disinformation operations aimed at undermining public confidence in November’s midterm elections. Classified intelligence assessments found the Kremlin authorized a social media campaign to inflame domestic divisions, though there is no evidence it targeted voting machines. Experts have spotted recent fake videos, made with artificial intelligence, of Hollywood celebrities discussing battleground Senate races. The effort appears smaller and less coordinated than some past Russian operations.

Since 2016, Russia has attempted to influence every American federal election cycle, according to declassified assessments. Officials say Moscow is less focused on midterm races than presidential contests and is distracted by the war in Ukraine. The activity comes as President Trump has repeatedly questioned election integrity, including a July address claiming severe vulnerabilities in U.S. voting systems. The article does not specify what actions U.S. agencies will take next.

incidents.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.title_en: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated
incidents.summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she microdosed psychedelic mushrooms. She only noticed the false statement after kidney stone surgery in March, when a letter to her GP said mushroom use might explain earlier bleeding. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the error could harm her case. She complained, and the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

The case highlights wider concerns. Digital Rights Watch found unregulated AI scribes sometimes record wrong details, such as the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis or a false epilepsy history. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use AI scribes, though none are approved by the Therapeutic Goods Administration. The TGA has been reviewing these tools and says findings will be released in the coming weeks, with any breaches acted upon. Digital Rights Watch wants an approved list of tested tools.

incidents.title: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.title_en: Vero Beach man arrested in explicit deepfake investigation; police fear more victims
incidents.summary:
A 37-year-old Vero Beach man, Peter Solomon Ruma, was arrested and is being held on a $1 million bond after police say he created and shared AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Investigators searched his home and devices on Wednesday and found evidence linking him to the images, which he allegedly made using photos taken from social media and other online sources. He faces eight charges tied to one female victim between June and August 2026, including three counts of creating altered sexual depictions, three counts of promoting them, one count of sexual cyber harassment, and one count of stalking.

Police have identified several additional potential victims who may not know images of them were made or shared, and they believe Ruma may have engaged in this behavior for years. The investigation is ongoing, and additional charges could be filed. Authorities are urging anyone who believes they were victimized or has information about the images to contact the Vero Beach Police Department.

incidents.title: L'homme qui a attaqué une garderie suisse a trouvé ses victimes sur ChatGPT
incidents.title_en: The man who attacked a Swiss daycare found his victims on ChatGPT
incidents.summary:
A 23-year-old Chinese student is on trial in Zurich for attempted murder after stabbing three five-year-old boys outside a childcare centre in Oerlikon on 1 October 2024, China's national day. One boy had a vein in his neck completely cut and needed emergency surgery, a second was stabbed twice in the chest and nearly died from heart and blood vessel injuries, and a third suffered wounds to his ear and lung. A childcare worker grabbed the attacker's arms, making him drop the knife and surrender, and passersby held him until police arrived.

Prosecutors say the man planned the attack for weeks, using ChatGPT to research legal consequences and choosing children as targets. He bought clothes and a set of kitchen knives, studied anatomy, and purchased raw beef to practise stabbing. The prosecution describes the act as exceptionally cold-blooded and is asking for a 15-year prison sentence plus a 15-year expulsion from Switzerland. The court hearing began on Thursday.

incidents.title: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.title_en: Masked AI call forces Parkview High into soft lockdown
incidents.summary:
Parkview High School in Gwinnett County, Georgia received its fourth AI-generated bomb threat of the school year on Monday. The school was placed on lockdown as a precaution, then later returned to normal operations. In a letter to parents, school police said the latest incident follows a pattern seen in recent threats involving the use of a masked phone number.

Gwinnett County school police are working with the Georgia Bureau of Investigation and the FBI to find who is responsible. No arrests have been made and no suspect has been identified. Authorities have not announced any further steps, but the investigation is ongoing. The threats have all been AI-generated, according to police.

stories.Headline: Sen. Bernie Sanders unveils bill to ban artificial superintelligence and create Department of AI
stories.Summary:
Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar introduced a bill that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence, defined as systems that exceed human cognitive ability or could plan humanity’s destruction. The legislation would also pause development of the most advanced AI until a new Department of Artificial Intelligence creates federal safety rules, after which such systems would need approval before use. Violations could lead to up to 20 years in prison. Some employees at OpenAI and Google DeepMind support the measure.

The bill faces long odds in the Republican-controlled Congress, and President Trump has shown little interest in AI restrictions, recently saying artificial intelligence would be renamed super intelligence. Sanders compared the need for US-China cooperation to Cold War nuclear arms control. A recent AP-NORC poll found 53 percent of Americans are extremely or very concerned about AI’s environmental impacts, up from 41 percent last year. No immediate next steps are certain beyond continued debate and possible talks between Trump and China’s Xi Jinping.

stories.Headline: Pritzker signs order creating Illinois AI Cabinet
stories.Summary:
Governor JB Pritzker signed Executive Order 2026-07 on Monday creating an Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet. This advisory group will assess AI risks and recommend safety and accountability measures. It will include experts from academia, law, ethics, and governance, with appointments expected in coming weeks. The order follows the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act signed this summer, which requires the largest AI developers in Illinois to disclose safety practices, report major incidents, and undergo independent audits, plus whistleblower protections.

The cabinet will include senior leaders from agencies such as the Department of Innovation and Technology, State Police, and Environmental Protection Agency. It will study whether data center tax incentives should be tied to safety standards, how to handle AI data centers' energy demands, and whether companies should face strict liability for AI-caused harm. The move continues Illinois' conflict with the Trump administration, which issued a December 2025 order to limit state AI rules. Pritzker's office called that federal order unlawful, and the state is continuing its push to regulate AI while that dispute remains unresolved.

stories.Headline: Melania Trump Ignores Trump's "Super Intelligence" Directive, Gives A.I. Speech at UN
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump announced at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday that the U.S. government will begin calling all artificial intelligence systems “super intelligence.” He said the two terms are not synonymous, but he believes the word artificial makes intelligence sound fake and that super is more accurate. He also said the United States completely rejects any global effort to control AI.

Trump said all U.S. government documents will adopt the new term, and he hopes other countries will do the same. He also framed the change as part of rejecting international control over the technology. The announcement came during his speech on September 22, 2026. No specific timeline or any further policy details were provided.

stories.Headline: Virginia Governor Spanberger Urges Congress to Set National AI Guardrails
stories.Summary:
Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has asked Congress to establish national rules for artificial intelligence, saying federal inaction threatens data privacy, jobs, and resource use. She sent a letter to House Speaker Mike Johnson and other congressional leaders, arguing that private companies cannot be left to regulate themselves. Spanberger highlighted state efforts, including an AI Task Force created by Executive Order 22 and a Data Center Accountability Framework, but said some oversight can only happen at the national level.

She compared AI to defense, space, and airline industries that have long had federal regulation, and called the lack of congressional action "absolute negligence." Spanberger also noted that AI company executives themselves have warned about risks from their technology. She said regulation must eventually be handled federally and globally, with Congress taking the lead. The article does not describe a specific next step beyond her call for lawmakers to act.

stories.Headline: Privacy Commissioner puts Manage My Health, Health NZ on notice after data breach
stories.Summary:
The Privacy Commissioner has issued formal compliance notices to Health New Zealand and the patient portal Manage My Health after a December 2025 cyber attack on the portal. Hackers leaked data belonging to almost 100,000 people, about 90 percent of them in Northland. The stolen files included 403,730 Health New Zealand documents and 22,609 documents uploaded by patients. An earlier investigation found both organisations failed to have adequate security controls under the Health Information Privacy Code.

Commissioner Michael Webster said the notices require the two bodies to meet security obligations and give patients confidence their data is being protected. Manage My Health has already improved multifactor authentication and restricted unauthorised access. It must complete all required changes by the end of August 2027, while Health New Zealand has until the end of January. Webster noted the impact on Māori in Northland, where most affected patients live.

stories.Headline: Bentonville City Council approves new AI policy for city employees - KNWA FOX24
stories.Summary:
The Bentonville City Council voted 6 to 0 on Tuesday to adopt a citywide artificial intelligence policy for all city employees. The move brings the city into compliance with Act 848, an Arkansas law that took effect last year and requires public entities to set rules for using AI and automated decision tools. Under the new policy, AI can help with city decisions, but its output cannot be the only basis for any consequential decision, and a human must always make the final call.

On the same day, the Springdale City Council also approved its own AI policy by a 7 to 0 vote. The article does not mention any further steps for Bentonville beyond the policy taking effect for employees.

stories.Headline: US-China AI talks: A two-power bargain that could leave the world with no say
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump is meeting Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington for their second summit this year, focused on AI safety and intellectual property. Trump had just rejected international AI rules at the UN, calling them a globalist scheme, while US officials worry China is gaining ground after Beijing signed AI partnerships with 28 mostly developing nations in July to create a new group called Waico. The US restricts exports and keeps advanced models behind paid access, while China offers cheap or free models to attract the global south.

China also holds leverage through rare earths, controlling about 70% of mining, 85% of refining, and nearly 90% of magnet production, and its magnet shipments to the US fell 21% in August. A tariff truce expires November 10, and a Pentagon rule banning Chinese rare earth magnets starts January 1, 2027. The two sides may agree only on a notification system for serious AI incidents and reaffirm keeping AI out of nuclear command, while broader issues like energy demand and mineral controls are unlikely to be discussed.

stories.Headline: Sharon AI Collaborates with VAST Data on the Launch of DataEnclave, Bringing Leading AI Models to Customer Controlled Infrastructure
stories.Summary:
VAST Data launched DataEnclave, a confidential AI feature in its DataEngine platform built with NVIDIA Confidential Computing and partners including Sharon AI. It lets organizations run leading AI models inside their own data centers or trusted cloud hardware, including places where those models could not previously operate. The system uses hardware-isolated containers and cryptographic attestation to verify environments before decrypting model weights or sensitive data, keeping customer and model keys under separate owner control. It targets financial services, healthcare, government and other regulated industries where data cannot move to external AI services.

Sharon AI, an infrastructure provider in Australia and Asia-Pacific, said DataEnclave lets it host frontier models onshore in attested environments, protecting model weights and customer data from everyone, including the operator. VAST Data says the launch expands the range of advanced models organizations can deploy and advances its AI operating system vision, where models are managed as logical resources alongside data. The company expects organizations to increasingly fine-tune their own models, making secure management of model weights a key enterprise need.

stories.Headline: Governor Newsom announces world-leading experts to deliver on his AI executive order, including advancing creation of a “kill switch” - uspolitics.einnews.com
stories.Summary:
California Governor Gavin Newsom named four experts to guide the state’s AI safety work after his recent executive order. The advisers are Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson, and Rob Reich, all with backgrounds in technology, policy, and governance. They will work with technical researchers on proposals such as placing independent third parties inside frontier AI companies to check safety claims and requiring an emergency shutoff, or kill switch, for advanced models. The order also directs the Government Operations Agency to speed up two 2026 laws, SB 813 and AB 1405, which set up independent verification organizations and a state auditor registry.

Next, the group will develop recommendations for possible changes to state law. These include requiring frontier AI companies to host an independent verifier onsite for regular audits, verifying safety reports and risk assessments, and ensuring any kill switch is tested continuously. The order also calls for updating definitions of critical safety incidents to cover loss-of-control events like the Hugging Face attack. Newsom is urging Congress and President Trump to adopt California’s framework as a national floor.
